These data have been used to determine augmentation flows from the Bal Creek upper reservoir that could be added to Howard Creek without raising the temperature above 20°C (Appendix J, Exhibit W). However, it may be more desirable to avoid increasing the water temperatures in Howard Creek over ambient levels, unless it can be shown that the detrimental impact on the trout fishery caused by flow reductions in Howard Creek warrants raising the temperature by augmenting flow with warmer water. If flow was augmented so that the temperature of the stream water did not go above that naturally occurring, the amount of augmentation would be at a lower rate than when flow was augmented until a maximum temperature of 20°C was reached.
Turbidity, dissolved solids and pH could also affect the use of upper reservoir water for flow augmentation. These parameters should also be monitored to determine the suitability of the water for release in Howard Creek. If water suitable for trout propagation could not be discharged during portions of the year, the system should be temporarily closed.
The Applicant's proposed erosion control plan, as described in Section 4 (See Appendix C), would provide protection from erosion and siltation for Howard Creek as well as Lake Jocassee and the Whitewater River. However, due to the highly erodable nature of the soils in the area, it is extremely important that the proposed plan be stringently implemented and the project and its access areas be continually inspected. Continual maintenance and control of access should be required. Figures 9-1 and 9-2 show the results of ground cover planting for erosion control on an untraveled and traveled logging road. Applicant should review the erosion control plan with the appropriate Federal, State, and local agencies and incorporate reasonable requests by the agencies for the protection of the aquatic environment. A suspended solids limit should be established for the effluent entering Howard Creek, Lake Jocassee, and the Whitewater River from erosion control structures. This limit should be established in consultation with the appropriate Federal, State, and local agencies.
